question: Chlorhexidine gluconate has persistent (residual) antimicrobial activity on the skin after a single application because it binds to the stratum corneum and is slowly released, maintaining antibacterial effect for up to 6 hours.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Chlorhexidine's substantivity (residual binding to skin) is its key clinical advantage: it provides 6-hour residual activity. Alcohol provides immediate kill but no residual activity, which is why chlorhexidine-alcohol combinations are preferred for surgical site preparation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Chlorhexidine's cationic nature enables binding to the negatively charged proteins of the stratum corneum. This substantivity (persistence) allows continued bactericidal activity after rinsing — a major advantage over alcohol-only preparations for surgical hand antisepsis and catheter site care.
